name: Dal Tadka
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi home and dhaba style)

ingredients.name: Split pigeon peas (toor dal / arhar dal)
Garlic (lahsun)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 3 cloves (2 chopped for masala, 1 sliced for tadka)

equipment: Small kadai or saucepan for the masala
Wooden spoon or whisk (mathani) to mash the dal
Measuring spoons and a ¼ cup measure

steps.title: Measure ¼ cup (50 g) toor dal into a bowl
steps.text: Measure ¼ cup (50 g) toor dal into a bowl
steps.visualCue: a small heap of yellow lentils
steps.videoShot: lentils pouring from the measuring cup into the bowl

steps.title: Rinse the dal in water 3 times, rubbing it gently with your fingers, and drain each time
steps.text: Rinse the dal in water 3 times, rubbing it gently with your fingers, and drain each time
steps.tip: if you have time, soak the dal for 20 min now. It cooks faster and softer.
steps.visualCue: the rinse water goes from cloudy to almost clear
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl showing clear water over the dal
steps.videoShot: a hand swirling dal in water, with cloudy water poured off

steps.title: Put the drained dal into the pressure cooker and add 200 ml water
steps.text: Put the drained dal into the pressure cooker and add 200 ml water
steps.visualCue: water about 2 cm above the dal
steps.cameraCheck: the open cooker with dal and water
steps.videoShot: water poured over the dal in the cooker

steps.title: Add ⅛ tsp turmeric and ¼ tsp of the salt to the cooker, and stir once
steps.text: Add ⅛ tsp turmeric and ¼ tsp of the salt to the cooker, and stir once
steps.tip: a drop of ghee in the cooker stops it from frothing out of the whistle.
steps.visualCue: the water turns pale yellow

steps.title: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 3–4 whistles
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 3–4 whistles
steps.visualCue: whistles counted, steam hissing
steps.cameraCheck: the closed cooker on the flame

steps.title: Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own
steps.tip: never force the lid open while there is still pressure.
steps.visualCue: the weight/valve drops and no more hissing

steps.title: Finely chop ½ small onion (40 g)
steps.text: Finely chop ½ small onion (40 g)
steps.visualCue: small even pieces about the size of a rice grain
steps.cameraCheck: the chopped onion on the board

steps.title: Finely chop ½ medium tomato (50 g)
steps.text: Finely chop ½ medium tomato (50 g)
steps.visualCue: small juicy cubes

steps.title: Grate ½ inch ginger (3 g), chop 2 garlic cloves, and thinly slice the third clove separately
steps.text: Grate ½ inch ginger (3 g), chop 2 garlic cloves, and thinly slice the third clove separately
steps.visualCue: two small piles, one chopped and one sliced
steps.videoShot: ginger rubbed on a grater, then garlic sliced

steps.title: Slit 1 green chilli lengthwise and chop 1 tbsp coriander leaves
steps.text: Slit 1 green chilli lengthwise and chop 1 tbsp coriander leaves
steps.visualCue: chilli split open, coriander finely chopped
steps.cameraCheck: chilli and coriander on the board

steps.title: Open the cooker and check that the dal is fully soft
steps.text: Open the cooker and check that the dal is fully soft
steps.tip: if it is still firm, add 50 ml water and give it 1–2 more whistles.
steps.visualCue: grains fall apart when pressed with a spoon, with no hard centre
steps.videoShot: a spoon pressing a lentil flat

steps.title: Mash or whisk the dal for 30 seconds until mostly smooth
steps.text: Mash or whisk the dal for 30 seconds until mostly smooth
steps.visualCue: a creamy, pourable texture with a few whole bits
steps.cameraCheck: the mashed dal in the cooker
steps.videoShot: the whisk spinning in the dal

steps.title: Heat 1 tsp (5 g) ghee in a kadai on medium heat
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp (5 g) ghee in a kadai on medium heat
steps.visualCue: the ghee melts and shimmers

steps.title: Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds (half of the 1 g) and let them crackle
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds (half of the 1 g) and let them crackle
steps.visualCue: the seeds sizzle and turn a shade darker, with a nutty smell
steps.videoShot: close-up of cumin bubbling in ghee

steps.title: Add the chopped onion and sauté until light golden
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and sauté until light golden
steps.visualCue: the onion edges turn golden and soft

steps.title: Add the ginger, chopped garlic and green chilli, and sauté
steps.text: Add the ginger, chopped garlic and green chilli, and sauté
steps.visualCue: the raw garlic smell is gone
steps.cameraCheck: the pan with aromatics mixed in

steps.title: Add the chopped tomato and a pinch of salt, and cook until soft and mushy
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and a pinch of salt, and cook until soft and mushy
steps.visualCue: the tomato breaks down and ghee shows at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the soft masala in the pan

steps.title: Pour in the mashed dal plus 50–75 ml water and stir
steps.text: Pour in the mashed dal plus 50–75 ml water and stir
steps.visualCue: the dal is pourable like thick soup, not a paste

steps.title: Add the remaining salt (to taste, about ¼ tsp) and simmer on low heat
steps.text: Add the remaining salt (to taste, about ¼ tsp) and simmer on low heat
steps.tip: stir from the bottom once a minute because dal catches easily.
steps.visualCue: slow bubbles on the surface and the masala blended in

steps.title: Stir in a pinch of garam masala and half the coriander, then turn off the heat and pour the dal into a serving bowl
steps.text: Stir in a pinch of garam masala and half the coriander, then turn off the heat and pour the dal into a serving bowl
steps.visualCue: green flecks in yellow dal
steps.cameraCheck: the dal in the serving bowl

steps.title: For the tadka, heat 1 tsp (5 g) ghee in the tadka pan on medium heat
steps.text: For the tadka, heat 1 tsp (5 g) ghee in the tadka pan on medium heat
steps.visualCue: the ghee shimmers
steps.cameraCheck: hot ghee in the tadka pan
steps.videoShot: ghee melting in the small pan

steps.title: Add the remaining ¼ tsp cumin and 1 dried red chilli
steps.text: Add the remaining ¼ tsp cumin and 1 dried red chilli
steps.visualCue: cumin crackles and the chilli puffs and darkens slightly
steps.cameraCheck: cumin and chilli in the pan

steps.title: Add the sliced garlic and fry until light golden
steps.text: Add the sliced garlic and fry until light golden
steps.tip: garlic goes from golden to burnt in seconds, so have the dal bowl ready beside you.
steps.visualCue: the slices turn pale gold, not brown

steps.title: Turn off the flame, then add a pinch of hing and ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
steps.text: Turn off the flame, then add a pinch of hing and ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
steps.tip: adding chilli powder off the flame stops it from burning and turning bitter.
steps.visualCue: the ghee turns bright red without darkening
steps.videoShot: chilli powder blooming red in the ghee

steps.title: Pour the tadka over the dal straight away
steps.text: Pour the tadka over the dal straight away
steps.visualCue: a loud sizzle and red ghee spreading on top
steps.cameraCheck: the dal with tadka on top
steps.videoShot: the sizzling tadka poured over the dal (hero shot)

steps.title: Garnish with the rest of the coriander and 1 tsp lemon juice if you like
steps.text: Garnish with the rest of the coriander and 1 tsp lemon juice if you like
steps.visualCue: a finished glossy bowl
steps.videoShot: coriander sprinkled over the finished bowl

reasons: the home version is a high-fibre, plant-protein dish with about 12 g of protein, little added fat (2 tsp ghee) and no frying or added sugar. Restaurant dal tadka often has 1–2 tbsp of butter or ghee plus cream or butter on top, more salt (often 1.5–2 g sodium) and sometimes a dhungar (charcoal smoke) finish, while the lentil content stays about the same.

researchRating.basis: dal tadka is one of India's most-cooked and most-searched comfort dishes. Top recipe pages are rated almost perfectly by readers, and comments consistently praise it as easy and restaurant-like. It loses a little because many people see it as an everyday, "plain" dish rather than a treat.

storage: Fridge: safe for 2–3 days in an airtight container. Freezer: up to 1 month, ideally frozen before adding the final tadka. Reheating: dal thickens as it cools, so add 2–4 tbsp water and reheat on the stove until it bubbles, or microwave for 1.5–2 min, stirring halfway. A fresh ½ tsp ghee tadka brings it back to life.
leftoverRemix: make dal paratha. Knead the thick leftover dal (about ½ cup) into atta with ajwain, chopped onion and coriander, using no extra water, then roll out and cook on a tawa with a little ghee. Alternatively, simmer the dal with cooked rice into a quick dal khichdi.
burnOff: Running: about 4.4 km at about 70 kcal per km. Walking: about 6 km at a brisk pace (est.), using about 50 kcal per km. With 2 rotis (about 530 kcal total): about 7.5 km running or about 10.5 km walking (est.).
